problem: Whether the variance V alone forces a universal lower bound on the normalized Turán deficit δ_k = 1 − f_{k−1}f_{k+1}/f_k^2 of a Poisson–binomial pmf near its mode, settled at the first-descent index D by proving V δ_D ≥ 1/4 when V ≥ 1.
debate: The literature on log-concavity and Turán/Newton-type inequalities for sums of independent Bernoulli variables, named on the page as ultra-log-concavity bounds (Hillion and Johnson), Johnson's probability-dependent bound, Dümbgen and Wellner's k-dependent bound, and the mode-location and maximal-mass results of Darroch, Pitman, and Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne.
gap: Every known lower bound on δ_k depends on n, on the success probabilities, or on k rather than on V, and all of them degenerate near the mode when summands with p_i near 0 and near 1 pile up at fixed variance, while the mode-location and maximal-mass results give no lower bound on δ_k at all.
contribution: A variance-scaled bound V δ_D ≥ 1/4 (V ≥ 1), with a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, consequences δ_k ≥ 1/(4V + |k − D|) everywhere and 1/(4V+1) ≤ δ_c < 2/V at the rightmost mode, an order-1/log N versus 1/N comparison for Haar unitary eigenvalue counts, and a proof that reduces to a one-variable inequality checked in exact arithmetic by Bernstein expansions.
note: The question is motivated only by a Gaussian 'natural scale' heuristic and one unitary-matrix example, so say early and plainly what a probabilist can do with this bound that the n-scaled bounds don't already give; expect referees to go after the unclosed 1/4 to 1/3 gap, the computer-assisted step, and why D in particular is the index that matters.
